endorsements.quote: An appropriate education allows health care professionals to be equipped with awareness of its risks and benefits, along with the necessary skills to identify, prevent, and address potential failures arising from its application in radiology [ 4 ].

Integrating AI into clinical engineering workflow in medical imaging entails structured interpretation sequences through strategic design of reading protocols to optimize diagnostic accuracy while counteracting cognitive biases [ 55 56 ].
Furthermore, XAI approaches can foster calibrated trust by enabling clinicians to interrogate the rationale and uncertainty of AI outputs rather than passively following algorithmic recommendations.
A fundamental consideration is providing comprehensive education on AI, increasing AI literacy, and enabling individuals to make informed choices [ 4 ].

unlisted_practices: Require radiologists to evaluate images independently before consulting past reports or AI interpretation outcomes.
Provide targeted training programs on cognitive biases, including structured explanations, simulation exercises and peer discussion of interpretative errors.
Establish clear communication strategies between clinicians and radiologists to prevent cognitive errors.
Conduct further research and develop structured guidelines to mitigate automation bias and other cognitive distortions in AI-assisted radiology.
Conduct external validation of breast imaging AI across diverse populations, risk profiles and imaging techniques such as digital breast tomosynthesis.

screen.reason: Viewpoint article discussing cognitive biases (anchoring, automation bias) in AI-assisted breast cancer imaging and outlining recommendations/strategies for mitigation and workflow integration.
